audit_findings.title: Celero’s post-close financing and economics are absent
audit_findings.magnitude: $625.0 million cash consideration, equal to 33.2% of the $1,882.0 million base equity value, plus unquantified seller expenses and adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: Celero's earnings and reinvestment requirements belong in OE, while acquisition interest expense belongs in equity-level OE and post-close cash, debt, assumed liabilities and contingent consideration belong in the bridge or financial-claims context
audit_findings.evidence: Acquisitions may also require additional financing or result in contingent liabilities, increased amortization expense, or asset impairment charges.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: the July 31, 2026 acquisition had closed before the September 6 valuation, but the valuation uses FY2025 OE and a June 30 pre-close balance sheet. The filed $625.0 million consideration is large enough to change the conclusion. The net direction is mixed because acquired earnings increase value while financing costs, integration spending, amortization and required reinvestment reduce it.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the closing statement, post-close debt draw, interest-rate schedule, seller-expense adjustments, assumed liabilities, contingent consideration, preliminary purchase-price allocation and Celero pro-forma financials; then rerun OE and the bridge on the post-close perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized commission buyouts may escape the owner-earnings reinvestment charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $36.0 million, equal to 27.4% of the $131.5 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If residual-commission amortization is added back while the separately classified investing cash outflow is excluded from maintenance investment, OE is overstated and that overstatement compounds through growth and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: We periodically enter into agreements with independent sales organization (ISOs) to acquire their rights to future commission payments.
audit_findings.explanation: The $36.0 million buyout and its capitalization are demonstrated, while its treatment in the OE calculation remains unresolved. Because the payment is 27.4% of anchor OE and management identifies the buyout as contributing to subsequent Merchant Services margin improvement, omission of a recurring maintenance component is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $36.0 million payment and subsequent amortization line by line to OE, obtain prior and expected future ISO buyout history, estimate the maintenance portion required to preserve merchant earnings, and rerun with either that cash cost deducted or the corresponding amortization retained.

audit_findings.title: The anchor still contains earnings from the disposed Safeguard channel
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.9 million first-half 2026 adjusted-EBITDA reduction, equal to 3.7% of the $131.5 million OE anchor; $22.8 million net sale proceeds, including a $12.0 million fair value of remaining proceeds receivable
audit_findings.mechanism: Disposed-channel earnings must be removed from anchor OE, while any sale consideration not already captured in June 30 cash must be recognized in the bridge; the $5.1 million sale gain is nonrecurring and should not enter OE
audit_findings.evidence: In February 2026, we entered into an agreement to sell certain assets and liabilities related to the small business distributor channel in our Print segment for approximately $25.0 million, with approximately half paid at closing and the remainder due over the next three years.
audit_findings.explanation: The stale earnings perimeter is demonstrated: Safeguard was sold in March 2026, and the filing quantifies a $4.9 million first-half adjusted-EBITDA reduction. The channel's actual 2025 OE contribution is not disclosed, but the demonstrated operating contribution and omitted receivable are reasonably capable of affecting the narrow gap between the $26.30 buy-below level and the $24.29 price. Removing earnings lowers value, while recognizing remaining consideration raises it.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Safeguard's 2025 revenue, operating profit, taxes, working-capital needs and maintenance investment; confirm that the $10.8 million cash receipt is already within June 30 cash; add only the unrecognized sale receivable or other retained claims, and rerun from a post-disposal OE anchor.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor contains a margin benefit management says will diminish
audit_findings.mechanism: A temporary vendor-rebate benefit embedded in FY2025 OE is grown and capitalized into terminal value unless removed before applying scenario growth
audit_findings.evidence: Looking ahead, while we expect continued benefits from our cost management initiatives and client diversification, we do not anticipate the same level of margin contribution from rebate programs in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The presence and subsequent diminution of the benefit are demonstrated: management identified incremental 2025 rebate benefits, and first-half 2026 Data Solutions margin fell 4.8 percentage points despite 23.8% revenue growth, with the filing attributing part of the decline to greater prior-year rebate favorability. The record does not isolate the rebate dollars from campaign mix and other costs, so materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the 2025 and expected recurring vendor-rebate amounts, reconcile them to cost of revenue and cash receipts, normalize FY2025 OE for the nonrecurring portion, and rerun all scenarios after normalization.

audit_findings.title: The dilution ceiling mixes a later share count with older outstanding awards
audit_findings.magnitude: 50.105 million modeled shares versus 46.4 million Q2 2026 diluted weighted-average shares, an 8.0% ceiling; using 46.4 million would raise base value to $40.56 per share and buy-below to $28.39
audit_findings.mechanism: Possible double-counting and maximum-award assumptions inflate the denominator and therefore reduce value per share without changing total equity value
audit_findings.evidence: Each RSU converts into one share of common stock upon completion of the vesting period.
audit_findings.explanation: The exact valuation-date diluted count remains unresolved, but the identified error is conservative. The modeled denominator is 8.0% above the filed Q2 diluted weighted-average count. Even the illustrative 46.4 million denominator would only raise base value and the buy-below threshold, leaving the $24.29 market price below the resulting $28.39 buy-below level. It therefore does not undermine the stated conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Roll the December 2025 option, RSU and PSU schedules through September 6, 2026, remove awards already vested or settled into the 45,856,290 July 31 outstanding shares, incorporate forfeitures and treasury-stock-method offsets, and update only the per-share denominator.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease asset replacement may fall outside reported capital expenditures
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.3 million of 2025 finance-lease amortization, equal to 1.7% of anchor OE; $51.4 million of first-half 2026 noncash finance-lease additions and $75.4 million of June 30 finance-lease liabilities
audit_findings.mechanism: If finance-lease asset amortization is added back but neither lease-financed replacement investment nor an equivalent maintenance charge is deducted, OE is overstated; ordinary principal must not also be deducted when the asset cost is already captured
audit_findings.evidence: We also utilize finance leases for our corporate headquarters and select information technology hardware.
audit_findings.explanation: The lease amounts are filed, but the OE treatment and maintenance portion are unresolved. The 2025 amortization alone is only 1.7% of anchor OE, while the much larger 2026 addition principally reflects a new 16-year facility and cannot be classified as maintenance from the record. The available evidence therefore cannot establish whether the valuation impact is material.
audit_findings.action: Trace finance-lease amortization, noncash additions and principal payments through the OE workbook; classify the headquarters and IT assets between maintenance and expansion; apply one nonduplicative maintenance charge, and rerun if the resulting recurring adjustment is significant.
